Fourteen comments

Follow Me Down (reel)

Source: Jackie Daly And Seamus Creagh by Jackie Daly And Seamus Creagh
Transcription: gian marco pietrasanta

↳ Posted by gian marco on June 14th, 2006.

This sounds like a reel version of the song, Follow Me Down (Up) to Carlow, which is usually sung with more of a polka swing to it.

↳ Posted by Will Harmon on June 14th, 2006.

Follow Me *Up*

Is it misnamed on the recording? A very similar but slightly different version of this tune appears on a couple of recent recordings. It is listed as “Bonnie Anne’s” on Angelina Carberry “An Traidisiun Beo”, and as “Lady Lubeck” on “Hidden Fermanagh Vol.1”

Related versions of the tune:
https://thesession.org/tunes/1583
https://thesession.org/tunes/4168

↳ Posted by slainte on June 15th, 2006.

From the sleeve notes of A. Carberry CD:
“The source of this first reel” is a collection of 105 tunes entitled ‘Oriel Songs and Dances’ published in the Louth Archaeological Journal“ of 1909 by folklorist the Reverend Luke Donnellan.”

From the notes of “Hidden Fermanagh” book on page 103:
“Lady Luebeck’s Reel: From ‘The Gunn Book.’ This is the same tune as for the song ‘Follow Me Up To Carlow’ by PJ McCall. The air is reputed to have first been performed by the pipers of Feagh MacHugh as he marched to attack Carlow in 1580…. However, it was also published in 1775 by Scots fiddler Daniel Dow as his own composition, ‘Bonnie Anne’. We have not been able to find any reference to the name ‘Lady Luebeck’.”

↳ Posted by slainte on June 15th, 2006.

It’s on Teada’s new album too

They play it as Follow Me *Down*: the identical version in Amin on A. Carberry CD and “Hidden Fermanagh Vol.1”, I believe. Check their website for the sound clip: http://www.teada.com

Follow Me Down, X:6

I was going through some old recordings I made during Angelina Carberry’s banjo class at Irish Arts week 2007.
I found a track where she demonstrated a beautiful variation of the Bonnie Ann tune. She first played her normal setting and the then the variation. They work well one after the other.
